summary: NPS-built 1934 two-story lookout at the highest lookout site in Mount Rainier National Park, now used for visitor services rather than full-time fire watch.

facts.design: two-story NPS rustic-style frame cab, 14x14 ft, balconied upper level with ground-floor storage

staffing.status: used for seasonal visitor services, not continuous fire detection

access.note: reached by trail from the Sunrise area of Mount Rainier National Park

events.note: built by NPS under Acting Chief Architect Edwin A. Nickel with Emergency Conservation Works Association assistance; Wikipedia text also states construction happened in 1933
added to NRHP March 13, 1991 as part of Mount Rainier National Historic Landmark District
registered on National Historic Lookout Register, March 31, 2003
windstorm tore the roof off; later repaired

evidence.supports: elevation, construction year, design, trail access, visitor-service use, recent restoration
evidence.quote: Constructed by the National Park Service in 1934, Mount Fremont Lookout is located at the end of a high, treeless ridge with outstanding views of Mt. Rainier. The two story frame building with 14'x14' live-in cab with catwalk is reached by a scenic trail and used by backcountry park rangers and was recently restored.

evidence.supports: elevation above 7,000 ft, highest in park, one of four remaining lookouts, visitor-service use
evidence.quote: The Mount Fremont Fire Lookout is a fire lookout in the northern region of Mount Rainier National Park at an elevation above 7,000 feet (2,100 m), the highest in the park. One of four fire lookouts remaining in the park, the lookout is used for visitor services during summer weekends.

evidence.supports: design, architect, construction detail, cables anchored to deadmen
evidence.quote: The building is about 14 by 14 feet (4.3 by 4.3 m), and was designed by the National Park Service Branch of Plans and designs under the supervision of Acting Chief Architect Edwin A. Nickel. It was built in 1933. The two-story structure features a balconied lookout on the second level, with storage on the ground level. Cables secured to deadmen keep the lookout from blowing over.
The Park Service was assisted during construction by the Emergency Conservation Works Association.
The lookout was extensively damaged in a 2006 storm, along with the park's Gobbler's Knob Fire Lookout. They've since been repaired.

evidence.supports: NRHP listing date, landmark district, rustic-architecture significance
evidence.quote: The lookout was placed on the National Register of Historic Places on March 13, 1991. It is part of the Mount Rainier National Historic Landmark District, which encompasses the entire park and which recognizes the park's inventory of Park Service-designed rustic architecture.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia's infobox says 'Built 1934' but its body text says 'It was built in 1933.' NHLR and firelookout.com both say 1934, so the story leads with 1934 and flags the 1933 claim as a minor internal conflict.

notes_for_editor: Minor internal Wikipedia inconsistency on build year (1933 vs 1934); not a cross-source conflict since NHLR and firelookout.com agree on 1934.
